speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned you have a limp and localized pain; can you tell me exactly where the pain hurts and how long this has been going on?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Since the pain is in the left knee but the limp suggests a problem higher up, does he also complain of pain in his left hip or thigh when you press there? Also, have you noticed any swelling or redness over the joint?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE). The presentation of a 7-year-old male with unilateral knee pain, limp, and no fever is classic for referred pain from the hip due to SCFE. I have reached my diagnosis limit and am ready to conclude.
